title: Leaving when Condon moved uptown, and tours of Germany and England
summary: When the downtown club closed he declined the uptown place and accepted his first European tour on his own, then an Alex Welsh tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay - well, then, that came to an end.
Well, it came to an end -- when the downtown closed that's when I decided that I didn't want to go to the uptown place. And, I had--- now, this is long after our tour---
In other words, before he closed downtown, he knew he was going to have an uptown place---
Yes, of course. And, I knew it too. But, I also had my first offer to go to England on my own and join the Alex Welsh Band and that was a tremendous band. And, I---
That actually came later but you had other offers -- you toured another part of Europe that time.
Yeah. The Alex Welsh thing came later.
Well, then it was Germany that I had the offer.
I had never been in Europe on my own-- and I grabbed this, whether it paid less or more. It didn't make any difference to me; I wanted to go. It turned out

that it was very successful for me, to go and also, I was very happy later when I was offered a chance to go to England and tour with one of the greatest bands in England. And, this proved to me - and I was hired by the same man - that hired the Condon band - that there was no malice as far as I was concerned.
That I did my job and they thought enough of me to ask me to come back, which I did.
Okay. So, then, you really went on your own after Condon moved uptown--
